sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a Leak

image.alt: Plumber checking a shutoff valve with a wrench

body: Tell us what you've noticed and where: a stain, a drip, a meter that keeps moving, a bill that jumped. If you can, tell us where your main shutoff is.
If water is running right now, shut it off at the main first, then call. We'll tell you what we think is going on and when we can get there.
Then we look for the source, not just the stain. Leak detection and camera inspections are part of the work. When we find it, we explain what it is and what it takes to fix.

sections.heading: Signs of a Leak You Can't See
body: Some leaks announce themselves. Others run quietly inside a wall or under the floor for a long time before anything shows.
You don't have to be sure it's a leak to call. If something is off, we'll look.

items.title: A water bill that jumped
items.text: Nothing changed in the house but the bill did. A slow leak runs all day and all night.

items.title: A warm spot on the floor
items.text: A hot water line leaking under a slab can warm the floor above it.

items.title: The sound of water when everything is off
items.text: Hissing or running water in a wall or under the floor, with every tap and appliance shut off.

items.title: Damp, stained or soft spots
items.text: A ceiling stain, a soft wall or floor, or a musty smell in a room that hasn't been wet.

items.title: Pressure that drops for no reason
items.text: Water escaping before it reaches the tap can show up as weak pressure.

sections.quote: Dan was very professional he came out this morning did a great job at fixing the pipe that was leaking. I would recommend him to anyone in need of plumbing. Thank you I appreciate you.

sections.heading: Where Leaks Hide
body: Some leaks are easy to reach: a supply line under a sink, a fitting at the water heater, an outdoor faucet. Others run inside a wall, under a slab or in the pipes leaving the house.

items.q: How do I know if I have a leak?
items.a: Watch for a jump in the water bill, a damp or soft spot, a warm floor or the sound of water with everything off. You can also turn off every tap and appliance and see whether the water meter still moves. If it does, call us.

items.q: Should I shut the water off?
items.a: If water is running and you can reach the main shutoff, yes. Then call us and tell us what you see.

items.q: Can you find a leak inside a wall or under a slab?
items.a: That's the kind of leak we go after. We can't say what we'll find before we look, but we'll tell you what we found and what it takes to fix before the work starts.

items.q: Do you fix the leak, or only find it?
items.a: Both. Finding it is the first half, and the repair is the second.
It depends on the leak and where it is. Ask us for the number before any work begins.

sections.heading: What Happens When You Call About a Water Heater

image.alt: Plumber checking a shutoff valve with a wrench

body: Tell us what the heater is doing: no hot water, a leak, a noise, rusty water. If you know, tell us whether it runs on gas or electric, and whether it's a tank or tankless.
We tell you what we think it is. Sometimes it's a part. Sometimes the tank is done. Either way, you hear it before you decide.
We take emergency calls from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., Monday through Saturday, based on availability. Hot water can't wait, so call early and ask when we can get there.

sections.heading: Signs a Water Heater Is Done
body: Most water heaters give warning first. A puddle, rust or a rumble is the heater telling you something.

items.title: Water around the base
items.text: A tank leaking from the bottom usually can't be repaired. Turn off the water to the heater and call.

items.title: Rusty or cloudy hot water
items.text: Rust in the hot water only can mean the tank is corroding inside.

items.title: Popping or rumbling
items.text: Often sediment built up in the bottom of the tank.

items.title: Little or no hot water
items.text: If the heater runs but the water never gets hot, a part may have failed. It isn't always the whole unit.

items.title: An old heater that's starting to act up
items.text: Water heaters wear out. If yours is old and the problems are stacking up, ask whether to repair or replace.

sections.quote: Dan and Jake were wonderful and replaced a rusty bolt on my hot water heater that was apparently defective after installation a year ago. Definitely live up to their high standards
sections.name: Susan D.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: Not every water heater problem means a new one. A failed part on an otherwise sound heater is a repair, and we'll say so.
A leaking tank, a rusted-out bottom or a heater that keeps needing work is where replacing starts to make sense. We lay out what we found and what each choice means, and you decide.
If you're replacing it, we'll go over size and fuel type and what fits your house.

sections.heading: Tank or Tankless
body: A tank water heater stores hot water and keeps it ready. A tankless heater heats water as you use it. We work on both.
Which one fits depends on your house, your gas line or power supply, and how much hot water you use. We'll go through it with you instead of pushing one.

sections.heading: Gas Water Heaters and the Gas Line
body: A gas water heater needs a sound gas line. Gas line installation, repair and replacement are part of what we do, so the heater and the line can be looked at together.
If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas company before anything else.

sections.heading: Before You Call
body: If the tank is leaking, shut off the water supply to the heater if you can reach the valve. Keep people and pets away from standing water around a gas or electric unit.
Then call and tell us what you see: where the water is, how much, and how old the heater is if you know. The more you can tell us, the better our read on the phone.
A heater that has gone cold may only need a part. Don't assume the worst until someone has looked.

items.title: We confirm what you have
items.text: Tank or tankless, gas or electric, and where it sits.

items.title: We shut it down
items.text: The water and the fuel or power to the old heater go off first.

items.title: The old one comes out
items.text: The new heater is set in place and connected.

items.title: We check it
items.text: We look over the connections for leaks and fire it up.

items.title: We walk you through it
items.text: You see what was done, and we leave the area neat.

items.q: How soon can you replace it?
items.a: Hot water can't wait, so ask when you call. Emergency calls are taken Monday through Saturday, 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., based on availability, and we'll tell you honestly what's possible.

items.q: Do you install tankless water heaters?
items.a: Yes, and tank heaters too. We'll talk through which fits your house.

items.q: Can you handle the gas line?
items.a: Yes. Gas line installation, repair and replacement are part of our work.
It depends on the heater and the house. Ask us for the number before we start, and we'll talk through what's included.

items.a: We do residential and commercial plumbing in Wichita and the surrounding area. Anything outside Wichita is subject to a trip charge.

why: Your homepage lists about 35 services on one page, and all five “MORE” buttons go to your contact page. Someone searching “leak detection Wichita” or “water heater replacement Wichita” has no page of yours to land on. Your page title leads with a tagline, “We'll get it within a foot!”, and your headline is only your company name.

Your customers already describe the company you are. Jenifer P.: “They found it and they took care of it.” Jeff S.: “They identified the leak areas that the gas company could not.” Today those words sit on Google, not on your site.
So the demo tells one story everywhere: a leak nobody could find, found and fixed. It opens with plumber in Wichita, KS, and gives leak detection and water heater replacement a page each.
